Phillip Peterson of the Council Auditor's Office explained the amendment; the amendment was unanimously approved by the Committee. 

Nina Sickler, Director of Public Works, explained that this bill moved funds from completed projects or projects that no longer needed funds to critically important projects that lacked funds. CM Boylan clarified that some of these projects "no longer needed" funds and were not necessarily completed but came in under the original budgeted amount. He asked whether the administration is continuing to seek out unspent dollars in previous appropriations; Ms. Sickler stated that it is.

CM Diamond congratulated the administration on finding projects that came in under budget, noting the rarity of this occurrence. He asked about the process for determining the projects that would be receiving these funds, and Ms. Sickler stated that these were high-priority projects at-risk of not being completed due to lack of funds. CM Diamond asked how programs were deemed "critical" or "high-priority," and Ms. Sickler answered that many of these programs were in underserved neighborhoods or were critical to City Resiliency plans. CM Diamond opined that this decision was a policy decision made by the administration to prioritize certain neighborhoods over others.

CM Boylan noted that the projects that needed these additional funds were running over their originally-appropriated amount; he asked whether projects in other districts also often ran over-budget.

• Approves a $6 million loan to developer in connection with the construction of a 100-unit mixed income housing complex as part of the personal property self-storage development located on the Southbank
• The loan will accrue interest at a rate of 1%, require interest only payments for a period of 18 years with the balance being due at the end of the loan term
• The loan will need to be funded at a later date and will be due upon project completion (estimated in 2027)
• The 100 units will be comprised of:
  - 5 units for households at or below 100% AMI
  - 75 units for households at or below 60% AMI
  - 20 units at market rate
• The loan will be secured by a second priority mortgage on the property of the multifamily component of the project
• The proposed loan is a result of a settlement agreement entered into between the City and the parties associated with the proposed Southbank self storage development. The settlement agreement requires consideration of the loan request, but does not require Council approval.
• The settlement agreement also requires consideration of a request for a $600,000 local preference loan (this has been approved by DIA and will be funded concurrent with the development’s receipt of a certificate of occupancy)

Jason Teal of the Office of the General Counsel gave some background information regarding this bill. The City Council previously had taken up a similar Planned Unit Development on this property with several companion bills including the disclaiming of an alley on the property, and the City Council voted to approve this PUD 9-9, which was interpreted as a denial of the PUD as this vote did not reach the majority needed to constitute an affirmative action of the Council. The applicant appealed the interpretation of the tie vote as meaning denial, there was a mediation process held between the applicant and the City, and both parties agreed to put a modified PUD along with companion bills before the Council. He explained that this settlement did not bind the City Council in any way.

Council Member Clark-Murray asked Mr. Teal whether this settlement would have any impact on how the Council proceeds, and Mr. Teal responded that the settlement agreed to place these bills before the City Council but that it was, for all intents and purposes, irrelevant to the City Council. 

Council Member Diamond asked the applicant's attorney, Steve Diebenow, to discuss the bill. Mr. Diebenow stated that he agrees that the City Council is not bound by the settlement but may want to consider elements of the settlement in its decision-making process. Public Hearing:

There were no speakers.

Edward Linsky of the Council Auditor's Office explained the amendment, which made the approval of this bill contingent upon the passage of the associated Planned Unit Development bill.

Council Member Carlucci stated that he was not in favor of approving a $6 million loan to the developer for the affordable housing portion of the project before the approval of the associated PUD bill. 

Council Member Clark-Murray noted that Committee needed to be objective in the passage of this bill, explaining the legal requirements for the City's abandoning of this alley. Council Member Carlucci explained that he had mixed up the bill associated with the alley closure and the bill associated with the affordable housing loan, given that they both had the same amendment (to make their approval contingent upon the passage of the associated PUD bill) attached to them. He asked whether the amendments for these two bills used the same language, and Mary Staffopoulos of the Office of the General Counsel explained that they did.

The amendment was unanimously approved by the Committee.
